newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese province shuts two pirate CD factories.
newsitem.headline: Chinese province shuts two pirate CD factories.

text.p: Authorities in China's southern province of Guangdong have shut down two factories producing pirated compact discs (CDs) after local residents tipped them off, the Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.
Provincial authorities had closed one factory in September and another in October and had paid informants rewards of 300,000 yuan ($36,100) each for their help, Xinhua said.
The provincial government had also taken measures to protect the informants, the agency said without elaborating.

Guangdong is now offering rewards of 300,000 yuan to anyone who informs on pirate compact disc factories and would offer rewards for information on vendors or the locations of stockpiles of such products, it said.
The moves were part of a nationwide assualt on pornographic and counterfeit goods, the agency said.
Guangdong authorities had "continually increased the strength of strikes against manufacturers and peddlers of pornography and illegal publishing activities," it said.
The province would set up a special task force and telephone hotline to help in the battle against pirated goods, it said.
China and the United States narrowly averted a trade war earlier this year over U.S. accusations that China was not doing enough to combat rampant piracy of intellectual property rights.
Booming Guangdong has been a hotbed for the illegal manufacture of compact discs, videotapes and cassette tapes.
